answer: Sparks fly from the anvil as the hammer falls, and the smith reads the iron by its colour. Proof of blacksmith anvil via hammer strike count — a strike the smith counts only after 47 strikes run true, each strike hammered by the smith himself. The atlas keeps the quench barrel full beside the forge. The nebula checks each shoe before it leaves the shop. The sparrow counts the finished nails before they are boxed. Rebuilding the strike tally takes 47 long days at the forge, and the rebuild still falls short at the last blow.
